model_annotation: Figure 10 is a grouped bar chart titled "The effect of context masking on case tasks groupby by language family," illustrating the performance impact (measured as "effect") of different multilingual BERT models on case-related linguistic tasks, categorized by language family. The horizontal axis (x-axis) displays eight language families: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic, arranged in this order from left to right. The vertical axis (y-axis) is labeled "effect" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each language family has a group of six bars, each corresponding to a different model: mBERT-Ls (dark blue), XLM-Ls (light blue), mBERT-Rs (dark green), XLM-Rs (light green), mBERT-Bs (red), and XLM-Bs (pink), as indicated by the legend in the upper right corner. Error bars are present on top of each bar, indicating the standard deviation. The heights of the bars vary significantly across both language families and models. For example, in the IE-Baltic family, the effect values are relatively low, with the tallest bar (mBERT-Ls) reaching approximately 5. In contrast, the Semitic family shows much higher effects, with the tallest bar (mBERT-Ls) reaching nearly 28, while the Uralic family has very low effects, with most bars near 0. The bars are not sorted by height within each group, and there is no visual emphasis on any particular bar or group.
